title: Portugal admitted to the United Nations
summary: Portugal joined the United Nations on 14 December 1955, in a package of sixteen admissions agreed between the Western and Soviet blocs to unblock a membership question that had been frozen since 1946. Membership had been vetoed until then, and the regime had treated the exclusion as evidence of hostility rather than as a problem to solve. Once inside, Portugal faced the opposite difficulty: from the late 1950s the General Assembly's anti-colonial majority made the African territories a standing item, and Lisbon answered by renaming them overseas provinces and denying that Chapter XI applied. It is in the atlas as the beginning of the diplomatic pressure that runs through the whole colonial war.
